Tech Jobs Through Time

How tech jobs emerged, changed and disappeared, from the human computers of the 1940s to the AI engineers of 2026: periods, role lanes, pay in real dollars, demand, layoffs, H-1B and India's workforce. US data is the backbone, with an India and global thread. Parts are published newest first.

🗓️ The periods

Tap a period to open its article. All ten periods are published.

🧑‍💻 Job lanes: born, peaked, faded

Consolidation view (AI, 2024–26): orange arrows = roles merging into one, teal = a new role splitting off, grey = a management layer removed. Tap a job for its source; arrows without a source are our reading. See the article.

Years run left to right along the top; each lane is a job family. Each job is one wave on its own line: it climbs while the job is rising (green), moves gently up and down while it is changing (blue), slopes down while shrinking (purple), and falls back to the line when it faded (amber) or is gone (red, ● = end year). Height is illustrative, not job counts. 2027–2030 (grey band, dashed) is an outlook: our reading of where each job is heading, not a forecast from data. Colour = today's state; dashed arrows = one role turning into another; paler waves = approximate dates (our reading). Scroll inside the map (the bar on the left scrolls the job lanes up and down, the bar on top scrolls the years): the years, job families and job names stay pinned. Moving dots flow along each job; green rings fire where a job is born, amber sparks burst at its peak, and a fading ember marks where it ended.

Tap a role for its story and source.

📈 The numbers

⚠️ = secondary source; est. = our estimate or arithmetic. Real dollars use US CPI-U annual averages. Data: data/tech-jobs-history.json. Disclosure: Claude, made by Anthropic, helps write this site.
